Subject: Re: Sudden tail queuing on reserved pool (EU cluster)

Hi Jonas —

We started seeing a spike in tail latency yesterday evening (2027-03-10 ~18:45 CET) on our dedicated GPUs in eu-west-1. A subset of inference jobs are being queued for multiple seconds even though we have a 32-GPU reserved pool and our observed concurrency hasn't exceeded the committed levels.

Impact: production recommendations (ranking) slowed by ~2–4s intermittently, affecting Timed Offers throughput. This is a material regression for our SLA-backed pipeline.

Can you confirm whether this was a scheduling change or an emergency maintenance? We need logs and an explanation of why the queueing behavior deviated from the documented reserved-queue priority.

Thanks,
Elena Rossi
Head of ML Ops
StratisAI

Subject: Re: Sudden tail queuing on reserved pool (EU cluster)

Hi Elena — thanks for the heads-up and for the logs.

Short answer: nothing scheduled that should affect reserved-pool priority, but we see evidence of transient KV-cache thrashing on a subset of nodes that correlates with bursts of long sequence jobs. That can cause short-lived queue buildup while the runtime rebalances prefix cache shards.

Immediate next steps we propose:
- Rishi (support) will pull per-node scheduling traces for the timestamps you provided.
- We can enable a temporary routing rule to route StratisAI traffic to a warm-hot carveout (no preemption) for the next 48 hours while we root-cause. This will avoid any contention from background batch work.
- If you prefer, we can roll a conservative guardrail to temporarily lower the per-request max-seq length to bound worst-case KV cache pressure (we'll do this only with your sign-off).

I'll let Rishi add technical details. Apologies for the interruption — we'll prioritize this and propose a short SLA amendment language if you want dedicated carveouts during incident windows.

— Jonas Weber
Director, Dedicated Capacity
Redwood Inference
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Sudden tail queuing on reserved pool (EU cluster)

Elena / team —

I dug into the submitted logs (thanks for sending). Quick findings:
- Between 18:37–18:52 CET we see a 70% increase in KV cache misses on nodes hosting your replicas. Misses are correlated with several requests with sequence lengths > 8k tokens (rare for you, but present).
- The scheduler honored reserved-slot affinity, but cache warming requires sequential token walks that briefly increase CPU and memory pressure and trigger our adaptive queue-depth limiter. The limiter purposefully queues non-latency-critical requests to preserve SLOs for pinned slots; that behavior looks like it protected throughput but produced observed queue delays for your occasional long-running requests.

I recommend two parallel actions:
1) Short-term mitigation (hours): enable the warm-hot carveout routing Jonas suggested. This gives you isolated capacity not subject to the adaptive queue-depth policy.
2) Medium-term (weeks): we can add a per-customer KV cache partitioning flag so your pinned capacity maintains a persistent prefix cache (avoids cross-tenant thrash). This requires an engineering rollout; I'll open a change ticket.

If you want the carveout, say the word and we'll schedule the re-route and measure.

Technical note (quoted):
> On Thu, 11 Mar 2027 09:12:45 +0100 Elena Rossi wrote:
> > We started seeing a spike in tail latency yesterday evening...

Rishi Malhotra
Sr. Technical Support Engineer
Redwood Inference

1) Schedule the routing change for 09:45 CET today.

3) Open an engineering ticket for persistent KV cache partitioning and share ETA.

Please reply with APPROVE to proceed or suggest edits to the amendment.
